graph-load.title: Graph load
graph-load.description: Read graph.json into bound VM collections (GraphLoader).

graph-layout.title: Layout (force / focus / hybrid)
graph-layout.description: Deterministic force/focus/hybrid layout with a quadtree; pins the focus node.

graph-build.title: Graph build
graph-build.description: Build the product-plus-code knowledge graph: containment, snaplinks, calls, hyperedges, communities.

graph-cache.title: Graph cache
graph-cache.description: Incremental, byte-deterministic graph cache keyed by per-file content hashes.

integrity-advisories.title: Coverage advisories
integrity-advisories.description: Non-gating declared-but-unlinked [CoversNode] advisories with one-click Add link.

integrity-relink.title: Re-point / remove link
integrity-relink.description: Fix an issue in place: pick a real target, or remove the link; rows re-bind after edits.

integrity-validate.title: Snaplink validation
integrity-validate.description: SnaplinkValidator: file/heading/class/method/url + node-link checks; unverifiable vs broken.

integrity-scan.title: Test-coverage reconcile
integrity-scan.description: Reconcile the [CoversNode] manifest against the tree: advisories, unknown-node, gating missing-snaplink.

graph-realise.title: Neighbourhood realisation
graph-realise.description: Realise the hop-radius neighbourhood (BFS) into the bound node/edge collections.

graph-lod.title: Zoom LOD
graph-lod.description: Level-of-detail: hide finer node/edge kinds as the canvas zooms out.

graph-cap.title: Node cap
graph-cap.description: Cap the realised node count, always keeping the focus, and report the remainder.

git-pull-result.title: Action Result Line
git-pull-result.description: Transient italic line under the bar reporting the outcome of a pull or a failed load; fades out after a few seconds.

git-worktree-mode.title: Worktree_mode
git-worktree-mode.description: State node - the controls that appear only when the open folder is a linked git worktree.

git-worktree-badge.title: Worktree Badge
git-worktree-badge.description: 'worktree' pill shown for a linked worktree, with a tooltip spelling out its merge and push state; its merged/unmerged and pushed/unpushed state is also appended to the status line. A broken remnant (dangling .git link) reads as an error.

git-worktree-remove.title: Remove Worktree
git-worktree-remove.description: Danger-styled 'Remove' button that deletes the worktree folder, prunes it and deletes its branch. A merged, clean worktree goes without a prompt; anything unmerged, dirty or broken confirms first, spelling out exactly what is lost.

git-read-service.title: Repository Reads
git-read-service.description: LibGit2Sharp-backed reads behind every display and every AI tool: working-tree status with ahead/behind, log, diff (working tree or staged), branches, a commit's message+diff, and remotes.

git-worktree-service.title: Worktree Detection & Removal
git-worktree-service.description: Detects a linked worktree (its .git is a file, not a directory), reports merge/push state against the mainline, and removes one - deleting the folder, pruning git's worktree record and deleting the branch. A dangling .git link yields a 'broken remnant' record rather than throwing, so it can still be cleaned up.

git-credentials.title: Credential Handling
git-credentials.description: Resolves push/fetch credentials by shelling out to the system credential manager (git credential fill), and stores a user-supplied access token (git credential approve) after the pull fallback captures one.

git-viewlet-match.title: Folder Match
git-viewlet-match.description: Which folders get a Git bar: GitViewlet matches a .git *directory* (a main checkout), GitWorktreeViewlet matches a .git *file* (a linked worktree's gitdir pointer). Mutually exclusive, and neither applies to a drive root.

dotnet-open-target.title: Open Target
dotnet-open-target.description: The ↗ button beside the target, always present so the affordance never moves, that opens the selected solution/project with its default OS handler (e.g. Visual Studio for a .sln/.slnx).

dotnet-target-scan.title: Target Discovery
dotnet-target-scan.description: Scans the open folder for .slnx / .sln / .csproj / .fsproj / .vbproj and orders them solution-first, so a folder holding both offers the solution as the default target.

dotnet-solution-reader.title: Solution Reading
dotnet-solution-reader.description: Parses a .slnx / .sln for its projects (skipping solution folders, resolving paths relative to the solution) and decides which are runnable - an exe/WinExe/Web SDK project, never a library or a test project.

dotnet-cli.title: Command Execution
dotnet-cli.description: Runs a dotnet verb as a child process, streaming its output back for the inline progress line and killing the whole process tree on cancel. `run` deliberately has no inactivity watchdog - a launched GUI app is legitimately silent.
dotnet-cli.note: Launches a real `dotnet` child process and manages its Win32 process tree - no seam to fake without reimplementing it. The guard paths (no target, cancel-while-idle) are unit-tested on the view-model; real execution is exercised by the app itself.

dotnet-startup-cache.title: Startup Project Memory
dotnet-startup-cache.description: Remembers which project the user chose to Run for a given solution, so the pick survives a folder revisit; a remembered project that is no longer runnable is discarded rather than honoured.

dotnet-nuget-check.title: Outdated Package Check
dotnet-nuget-check.description: Background `dotnet list package --outdated` for the selected target, cached for a day and re-run on target switch and after a restore/build. Runs from a neutral working directory so it never locks the folder, and a debounce means folders merely passed through are never checked.
dotnet-nuget-check.note: Shells out to a real `dotnet list package --outdated` against a restored target - too slow and network-dependent for a unit test. Its result handling (the caution badge, the tooltip, clearing when nothing is outstanding) is unit-tested via dotnet-nuget-caution.

dotnet-viewlet-match.title: Folder Match & Quiesce
dotnet-viewlet-match.description: Which folders get a .NET bar (one holding a .slnx/.sln or a project file), and releasing the folder on demand: the NuGet check is cancelled and any running verb's process tree is killed, so the folder can be renamed or deleted (e.g. by a git worktree removal).
dotnet-viewlet-match.note: The glob match is declarative registration data and the quiesce path kills a live child process tree; neither has VM state to assert. Presence of the bar for a solution folder is covered by the UI journey.

font-ui.title: UI
font-ui.description: Everything the user sees or touches in the Font tab: the preview top bar, the compare list, the details panel for the selected font, and the add-a-font picker overlay.

copy-name.title: Copy Name
copy-name.description: Copies the selected font's display name to the clipboard.
copy-name.note: The unit test covers the guard (nothing selected copies nothing). The clipboard write itself is a single WPF call wrapped in try/catch - the clipboard can be locked by another process - and needs an interactive desktop, so it is exercised by the UI journey.

select-font-style.title: Face Variant Chips
select-font-style.description: Chip strip of the family's faces (Regular / Bold / Italic / ...); picking one re-renders that font's preview row in that face and repoints the metadata rows and glyph map at it.

view-glyph.title: Glyph Grid
view-glyph.description: The paged grid of the face's mapped characters, rendered in that face. Capped per page so a large CJK font never realises tens of thousands of cells, with Prev / Next and a page label.

copy-glyph.title: Copy Glyph
copy-glyph.description: Clicking a glyph cell copies that character to the clipboard, like Character Map.
copy-glyph.note: The unit test covers the guard (an empty cell copies nothing). The clipboard write itself needs an interactive desktop and is exercised by the UI journey.

font-functionality.title: Functionality
font-functionality.description: Behaviours behind the viewer that are not a UI control or an AI tool: how a font file is turned into something WPF can render, and the entry points that open the tab.

list-panel.title: List Panel
list-panel.description: The left-hand surface: one preview row per chosen font, with the add-a-font button beneath.

add-font.title: Add Font
add-font.description: Button under the compare list that opens the font picker overlay to add another font to compare.

font-details-2.title: Metadata Rows
font-details-2.description: The grouped detail rows read from the selected face's GlyphTypeface: identity, style and metrics, legal / licensing and technical fields. A font that failed to load shows its error here instead.

font-selected.title: Font Selected
font-selected.description: State node - the panels that only have anything to show once a font in the compare list is selected.

topbar.title: Topbar
topbar.description: The top bar spanning the tab: the editable preview string and the size slider that restyle every compare row at once.

size-slider.title: Size Slider
size-slider.description: 8-120pt slider setting the preview size for every row at once, snapped to whole points and shown beside the slider. WPF renders in DIPs, so the value is converted (pt x 4/3) for the previews.

font-text-display.title: Preview Text
font-text-display.description: The editable sample string, applied live to every row in the compare list as it is typed.

remove-font.title: Remove Font
remove-font.description: Per-row close button that drops that font from the compare list, reselecting a neighbour so the details panel is never left showing a font that is gone.

copy-path.title: Copy Path
copy-path.description: Copies the selected font's file path to the clipboard. Does nothing for an installed system font, which has no source path of its own.
copy-path.note: The unit test covers the guard (an installed family has no source path, so nothing is copied). The clipboard write itself needs an interactive desktop and is exercised by the UI journey.

font-decode-pipeline.title: Decoder registry
font-decode-pipeline.description: The generic half: FontSourceResolver asks each registered IFontFormatDecoder whether it handles the extension, writes the decoded bytes to a temp file and hands back a Uri, cleaning the temp files up on dispose. A file needing no decoding is passed through as-is. Adding WOFF2 is one more decoder plus a filemap line - no change here.

font-decode-woff.title: WOFF decoder
font-decode-woff.description: The one format implemented today: parses the WOFF header and table directory and zlib-inflates each compressed table back into an sfnt WPF can load. WOFF2 is a future sibling (Brotli plus table-transform reversal).

winfs-keyboard-open.title: Open Selected (Shift+Enter)
winfs-keyboard-open.description: Shift+Enter opens the selected entry via the same OpenEntryCommand the row's double-click binding uses: folders navigate, files go through the default-open resolver. Shift-modified because the AI input holds focus and owns plain Enter. Single selection only.

git-ai-act-git-log-ranges.title: Revision ranges & filters
git-ai-act-git-log-ranges.description: git_log gains a revision range (A..B) plus --since/--until/--author/--grep/--no-merges. Without a range the tool can only walk back from a tip, so 'what changed between two releases' cannot be expressed at all; the 200-commit cap makes tip-walking unusable at release scale.

git-ai-act-git-diff-refs.title: Two-ref diff & output format
git-ai-act-git-diff-refs.description: git_diff gains from/to revisions (tags, branches, hashes) and a format switch: stat | name-only | patch. Today it only diffs uncommitted work, and always returns full patch text capped at 600 lines - useless at release scale, where a --stat summary is the only readable first answer.

git-ai-act-git-tags.title: git_tags
git-ai-act-git-tags.description: List tags (optionally matching a pattern) with their target commit and date, plus describe for the nearest tag to a ref. Nothing in the surface exposes tags today, so the assistant cannot even discover that a release boundary such as v1.3.0 exists.

git-ai-act-git-file-at.title: git_file_at
git-ai-act-git-file-at.description: Read a file's contents as of any revision (git show <rev>:<path>). The only way to answer 'what did this config/default look like before' - currently impossible, since every read is against the working tree.

git-ai-act-git-merge-base.title: git_merge_base
git-ai-act-git-merge-base.description: Merge base and ahead/behind counts between two ARBITRARY refs. git_status only reports ahead/behind against the current branch's upstream, so 'how far is this branch from main' is unanswerable.

git-ai-act-git-contains.title: git_contains
git-ai-act-git-contains.description: Which branches and tags contain a given commit, and whether ref X is fully merged into ref Y. This is the 'is it safe to delete this branch' question, and the honest answer to 'did we lose that work'.

git-ai-act-git-blame.title: git_blame
git-ai-act-git-blame.description: Line-by-line authorship and last-touching commit for a file or line range, so the assistant can answer 'who changed this and why' and follow the trail into the commit message.

git-ai-act-git-search-history.title: git_search_history
git-ai-act-git-search-history.description: Search history rather than the working tree: pickaxe -S/-G for when a string appeared or vanished, and --grep over commit messages. Answers 'when did we stop doing X' - today only the current checkout is searchable.

git-ai-act-git-recovery.title: git_recovery
git-ai-act-git-recovery.description: List stashes, and read the reflog. The recovery surface: reflog is what proves nothing was lost after a branch delete, reset or bad merge, and it is the only place work that is not on any branch still shows up.

git-ai-act-git-worktrees.title: git_worktrees
git-ai-act-git-worktrees.description: Enumerate every linked worktree of the repo with its branch, dirty/unpushed/merged state and whether it is a broken remnant. GitWorktreeService already computes all of this, but only for the folder currently open - the assistant cannot see the others.

git-ai-act-forge.title: Forge integration (PRs & issues)
git-ai-act-forge.description: Read pull requests and issues from the repository's hosting forge, behind a provider abstraction: GitForgeClient carries no forge-specific knowledge, and each backend (host match, URL shapes, auth, JSON mapping) is one IGitForgeProvider in GitForgeRegistry. Supporting another forge is a new provider plus a registry line - nothing in the client or the tools changes.

git-ai-act-git-compare.title: git_compare
git-ai-act-git-compare.description: One call for 'what is the difference between A and B': ahead/behind counts, the changed-file stat, and the commit list. Directly answers the release-comparison question the current surface fails.

git-ai-act-git-changelog.title: git_changelog
git-ai-act-git-changelog.description: Release notes for a range: non-merge commit subjects PLUS merged pull-request titles, grouped, with a file-stat summary and contributors. The tool that writes WhatsNew.md - assembled by hand from six commands on 2026-07-22.

git-ai-act-git-branch-audit.title: git_branch_audit
git-ai-act-git-branch-audit.description: Every branch with upstream, whether the upstream is gone, commits not on the mainline, whether a worktree holds it, and any backing PR. The whole 'is this safe to prune' review in one call, instead of a nervous five-command dance.

git-ai-act-git-find-work.title: git_find_work
git-ai-act-git-find-work.description: Find work by topic across branches, tags, stashes, reflog and remote PRs - the 'where did that change go' question. High user value: work removed with its worktree looks deleted while being perfectly safe, and this is what proves it.

git-ai-act-git-file-history.title: git_file_history
git-ai-act-git-file-history.description: Commits touching a path, following renames, with the option to fetch the file's content at any of them. Combines git_log --follow with git_file_at so a file's evolution is one call rather than N.

git-ai-act-forge-prs.title: git_pull_requests
git-ai-act-forge-prs.description: List pull requests from GitHub or Bitbucket - state filter, title search, source/target branches and author. PR titles are the best release-note material there is, and a PR is often the only surviving record of why a branch exists.

git-ai-act-forge-issues.title: git_issues
git-ai-act-forge-issues.description: List issues from GitHub or Bitbucket. GitHub's issues endpoint also returns pull requests; those are dropped so the two tools do not double-report.

git-ai-act-forge-providers.title: Providers
git-ai-act-forge-providers.description: The forge backends registered in GitForgeRegistry. Each is one IGitForgeProvider - host match, repo-path parsing, endpoint URLs, auth scheme and JSON mapping. Add a node here when adding a provider so the supported set stays visible in the tree.

git-ai-act-forge-github.title: GitHub
git-ai-act-forge-github.description: GitHub (and Enterprise hosts named *github*): owner/repo paths, bearer-token auth, bare-array listings with head.ref / base.ref branch fields; drops PRs from the issues endpoint.

git-ai-act-forge-bitbucket.title: Bitbucket
git-ai-act-forge-bitbucket.description: Bitbucket Cloud: workspace/repo paths, basic auth (x-token-auth access tokens), values-wrapped pages with source.branch.name / destination.branch.name; caps-and-repeated state vocabulary.

git-ai-act-forge-azure.title: Azure DevOps
git-ai-act-forge-azure.description: NOT YET BUILT. Azure DevOps: org/project/_git/repo paths (three levels - GitForgeRepo.Project already models this), basic auth with a PAT, and its own PR/issue (work-item) JSON. Add a GitForgeProvider + a GitForgeRegistry line; the extension point is proven by the FakeAzureProvider test.

git-ai-act-forge-abstraction.title: Provider abstraction
git-ai-act-forge-abstraction.description: IGitForgeProvider + GitForgeRegistry: the seam that keeps GitForgeClient forge-agnostic. A provider passed to the client is used with no other change - proven by ANewProvider_PluggedIn_IsUsedWithoutTouchingTheClient.

dicom.title: DICOM
dicom.description: Viewer-only DICOM (medical imaging) tab: lists a DICOMDIR/folder/single-file container as a Patient>Study>Series>Instance tree and views images in-page with zoom/pan, window/level, cine and measurement. Reports open in their normal viewer with a breadcrumb back here. Built on fo-dicom (+ native codecs).

dicom-load.title: Container Loading
dicom-load.description: Turns a DICOMDIR index, a folder of loose instances, a single .dcm, a multi-file selection or an archive browsed as a folder into one Patient>Study>Series>Instance tree, read off the UI thread. A series is ordered by instance number and its images cross-linked so the wheel can step them; an instance that fails to parse is reported as a warning rather than failing the load.

dicom-image-pane.title: Image Pane
dicom-image-pane.description: The stage the selected frame is drawn on, with the measurement overlay and the corner readouts above it. The frame carries the zoom/pan transform; the overlay is redrawn in screen space rather than transformed, so annotation strokes stay one width at any zoom.

dicom-window-level.title: Window / Level Drag
dicom-window-level.description: Right-drag sets brightness and contrast: horizontal moves the window width, vertical the centre. Width is floored at 1 so the mapping can never collapse.

dicom-cine.title: Cine Transport
dicom-cine.description: The bar under the stage, present only for a multi-frame image: play/pause, frame step and a frame slider. The timer stops when the tab is deactivated or the window minimised so a background tab is not decoding frames.

dicom-measurements.title: Measurement Overlay
dicom-measurements.description: Length and angle, and rectangle/ellipse ROIs with area and - on CT - HU mean and SD. Distances are millimetres when the image declares PixelSpacing and pixels when it does not. Points are stored in image space so they re-project under any zoom.

dicom-reports.title: Encapsulated Reports
dicom-reports.description: An encapsulated document - typically a PDF report - is extracted to a temp file and opened in its normal viewer. The spawned tab's breadcrumb points back at this DICOM page rather than at the throwaway temp directory, and the temp files are deleted when the tab closes.

dicom-hide-patient.title: Hide Patient Toggle
dicom-hide-patient.description: One click masks the patient identifiers in the tree labels, the overlay line and the tag values. Patient info is shown by default - this is a viewing choice, not the AI boundary, which withholds identifiers regardless.

dicom-ai.title: AI Integration
dicom-ai.description: How the assistant sees and acts on this page. The boundary is the point of it: context and every tool report de-identified study, series and geometry only, and the page declares a raised security risk so a pinned DICOM tab is never treated as ordinary content.

dicom-tag-drawer.title: Tag Drawer
dicom-tag-drawer.description: Collapsible right-hand panel, closed by default and resizable by its splitter, listing the selected instance's tags. Its width survives a close and re-open.

text-viewer-replace.title: Replace
text-viewer-replace.description: Replace the current match, or Replace All across the file; auto-enters editing (disabled on non-editable files).

text-viewer-match-case.title: Match Case
text-viewer-match-case.description: Match-case (Aa) toggle in the Find & Replace bar; threads case-sensitivity through the search engine.

text-viewer-regex.title: Regex
text-viewer-regex.description: Regex (.*) toggle in the Find & Replace bar; runs the search as a regular expression.

text-viewer-goto-line.title: Go to Line
text-viewer-goto-line.description: Go to line (Ctrl+G / toolbar): prompts for a line number and scrolls/slides to it.

text-viewer-undo-redo.title: Undo / Redo
text-viewer-undo-redo.description: Multi-level undo/redo while editing (Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y + toolbar buttons), backed by AvalonEdit's document undo stack.

text-viewer-zoom.title: Zoom
text-viewer-zoom.description: Editor zoom in the footer: preset popup (80-130%) plus Ctrl+wheel / Ctrl+plus/minus / Ctrl+0.

markdown-ui.title: UI
markdown-ui.description: Everything the user sees or touches in the Markdown editor tab.

markdown-functionality.title: Functionality
markdown-functionality.description: Behaviours the Markdown editor performs that are not a UI control or an AI tool.

markdown-document.title: Document Surface
markdown-document.description: The document region under the toolbar: two surfaces over the same text (rendered inline editor / raw source box) swapped by the Source toggle.

markdown-fmt-clipboard.title: Clipboard buttons
markdown-fmt-clipboard.description: Cut / Copy / Paste icons in the mini-toolbar's first row; Cut is disabled without a selection and Paste when the clipboard holds nothing usable.
markdown-fmt-clipboard.note: Cut/Copy/Paste drive the RichTextBox selection + the system clipboard — no view-model state to assert. Presence and enablement are covered by the UI journey.

code-ui.title: UI
code-ui.description: Everything the user sees or touches in the As Code tab.

code-functionality.title: Functionality
code-functionality.description: Behaviours the As Code tab performs that are not a UI control or an AI tool.

code-change-banner.title: External-change banner
code-change-banner.description: Accent banner over the editor after the file changed on disk and was reloaded; auto-dismisses after 3 seconds. The reload itself (and the prompt when there are unsaved edits) is the file-watch behaviour.

code-status-filesize.title: File size
code-status-filesize.description: Footer label showing the file's on-disk size, refreshed after a save or an external-change reload.

code-status-state.title: Unsaved / read-only indicators
code-status-state.description: Footer flags: an amber '● unsaved' while the buffer differs from the saved state, and 'read-only' when the file opened over the editable-size ceiling or failed to open.

code-structure.title: Structure extraction
code-structure.description: Tree-sitter extraction of the file's outline (imports, types, members, embedded regions) from the live buffer, debounced on edit, and the stable AST paths that keep code-map links valid across edits.

tabular-ui.title: UI
tabular-ui.description: Everything the user sees or touches in the Tabular tab.

tabular-functionality.title: Functionality
tabular-functionality.description: Behaviours the Tabular tab performs that are not a UI control or an AI tool.

tabular-toolbar.title: Toolbar
tabular-toolbar.description: Top bar: the detected-shape descriptor, a how-to hint, a transient status message, and the two template buttons pinned right.

tabular-encoding-label.title: Encoding label
tabular-encoding-label.description: Footer readout of the encoding the file was decoded with (from the BOM/UTF-8 sniff).

tabular-mode-label.title: Small/large mode label
tabular-mode-label.description: Footer note telling the user which reading mode the file opened in — small files load whole (sort enabled), large files stream through a row window (sort disabled).

tabular-shape-label.title: Detected-shape descriptor
tabular-shape-label.description: Reads back how the file was interpreted — separator, quoting, header row and column count — so a mis-detection is visible before the user trusts the grid.

tabular-toolbar-template-this.title: Template This button
tabular-toolbar-template-this.description: Opens the Template This popup, seeded with the file's name, folder and an extension glob.

tabular-toolbar-apply-template.title: Apply Template button
tabular-toolbar-apply-template.description: Toggles the Apply-Template side panel open and closed.

tabular-template-name.title: Template name
tabular-template-name.description: Name box for the saved template; Save stays disabled while it is blank.

tabular-template-scope.title: Scope choice
tabular-template-scope.description: Folder / filename-glob / manual-only radio group deciding when the template auto-applies; the glob scope additionally requires a pattern.

tabular-template-save.title: Save
tabular-template-save.description: Captures the live transform chain as a template and persists it to the Tabular Templates config.

tabular-template-apply.title: Apply a template
tabular-template-apply.description: Applying a listed template replaces the live transform chain with its own; an incompatible template is confirmed first.

tabular-show-only-compatible.title: Show only compatible
tabular-show-only-compatible.description: Switch that filters the list to templates whose captured shape matches this file; rebuilds the list on every flip.

tabular-template-delete.title: Delete template
tabular-template-delete.description: Hover-revealed ✕ on a listed template: removes it from the saved set and rebuilds the list.

tabular-template-panel-close.title: Close panel
tabular-template-panel-close.description: ✕ in the panel header; closes it without applying anything.

win-registry-ui.title: UI
win-registry-ui.description: Everything the user sees or touches in the Registry tab.

win-registry-functionality.title: Functionality
win-registry-functionality.description: Behaviours the Registry tab performs that are not a UI control or an AI tool.

registry-input-prompt.title: Input prompt
registry-input-prompt.description: The in-tab text prompt every naming/data action routes through (new key, rename, new value, modify value): OK hands the typed text to the pending action, Cancel discards it, and the callbacks are one-shot so a stale one can never fire against a later key.

registry-confirmation.title: Delete confirmation
registry-confirmation.description: The in-tab confirmation gating every destructive action (delete key, delete value); names the exact target and runs nothing until Delete is pressed.

windowsapps-ui.title: UI
windowsapps-ui.description: Everything the user sees or touches in the Installed Apps tab.

windowsapps-functionality.title: Functionality
windowsapps-functionality.description: Behaviours the Installed Apps tab performs that are not a UI control or an AI tool.

processes-ui.title: UI
processes-ui.description: Everything the user sees or touches in the Processes tab and the per-process details tab.

processes-functionality.title: Functionality
processes-functionality.description: Behaviours the Processes feature performs that are not a UI control or an AI tool.

processes-header.title: Header
processes-header.description: Title row: the shown/total process counts and the system CPU + RAM sparkline gauges.

processes-counts.title: Process counts
processes-counts.description: 'N shown · M total' — the filtered row count against every running process, so a filter can never be mistaken for a system with fewer processes.

processes-refresh-now.title: Refresh now
processes-refresh-now.description: Re-samples the process list immediately, independently of the live toggle.

processes-view-details.title: View details
processes-view-details.description: Opens the per-process details tab for the clicked row, seeded with its PID.

details-kill.title: Kill (details)
details-kill.description: Terminates the process being inspected, behind the same confirmation the list's row menu uses.

processes-cpu-sampling.title: CPU sampling
processes-cpu-sampling.description: Turns raw per-process kernel/user time deltas into a 0-100% figure scaled by core count, clamped so a burst over budget can't read above 100.

processes-reconcile.title: Snapshot reconciliation
processes-reconcile.description: Folds each fresh snapshot into the live row set in place — same PID keeps the same row instance (so selection, expansion and scroll survive), dead processes drop out, metrics update without rebuilding the list.

processes-tree-build.title: Process tree building
processes-tree-build.description: Nests each process under its parent, promoting orphans and PID 0/4 children to roots and refusing to recurse forever on a mutual- or self-parent cycle.

processes-live-source.title: Live process source
processes-live-source.description: The system sampler behind the tab. Snapshot() and ReadDetail() are driven from background threads, so its caches are serialised — an unsynchronised dictionary corrupted itself here before.

sysinfo-ui.title: UI
sysinfo-ui.description: Everything the user sees or touches across the SysInfo tabs — the dashboard, the Services page and the Environment Variables page.

sysinfo-functionality.title: Functionality
sysinfo-functionality.description: Behaviours the SysInfo feature performs that are not a UI control or an AI tool.

log-viewer-ui.title: UI
log-viewer-ui.description: Everything the user sees or touches in the log tab: the toolbar, the read-only log pane, the filter side panel and the status bar.

log-viewer-functionality.title: Functionality
log-viewer-functionality.description: What the viewer does behind the controls: streaming a large file tail-first, following appends, sniffing the encoding, picking a parser and detecting timestamps.

log-viewer-filter-panel.title: Filter Panel
log-viewer-filter-panel.description: Always-visible right-hand side panel holding the regex pattern box and, when the log carries timestamps, the From/To time range fields. Both fade non-matching lines rather than removing them.

log-viewer-statusbar.title: Status Bar
log-viewer-statusbar.description: Bottom strip reporting loaded line count, file size, the detected log format, the active filter and a history-loading indicator while the head streams in.

log-viewer-line-select.title: Line Selection Margin
log-viewer-line-select.description: Clickable left margin: clicking a line toggles whole-line selection and copies the selection straight to the clipboard; selected lines stay washed as you scroll.

log-viewer-filter-clear.title: Clear Filter
log-viewer-filter-clear.description: The X beside the pattern box, shown only while a filter is active; clears the pattern and un-fades every line.

log-viewer-time-apply.title: Apply Time Range
log-viewer-time-apply.description: Combines each date with its time box into a filter bound, fades lines outside the range and scrolls to the first line inside it. A To date with no time means end-of-day.

log-viewer-time-clear.title: Clear Time Range
log-viewer-time-clear.description: Empties the From/To fields and drops the time bounds, so every line un-fades.

log-viewer-status-lines.title: Line Count
log-viewer-status-lines.description: Count of lines currently in the document - the tail only, until the head finishes streaming in.

log-viewer-status-size.title: File Size
log-viewer-status-size.description: The file's size, re-formatted as the file grows under the live tail.

log-viewer-status-format.title: Detected Format
log-viewer-status-format.description: Name of the parser the registry voted for (JSON lines vs raw text).

log-viewer-status-filter.title: Active Filter Indicator
log-viewer-status-filter.description: Shows the live regex pattern in the warning colour while a filter is fading lines, so a filtered view is never mistaken for the whole log.

log-viewer-status-loading.title: History-Loading Indicator
log-viewer-status-loading.description: Loading history spinner shown while the head of a large file is still being reassembled behind the already-readable tail.

log-viewer-encoding-detect.title: Encoding Detection
log-viewer-encoding-detect.description: Sniffs the file with the shared EncodingDetector (BOM, UTF-8 validity, UTF-16 heuristic) off the UI thread before any text is read, so every viewer agrees on the encoding.

log-viewer-timestamps.title: Timestamp Detection
log-viewer-timestamps.description: Votes on whether the log is timestamped by sampling the first 20 lines through the parser that was just selected - a JSON log carries its timestamp in a field, so a text-shaped probe would decide the file has none and hide the time filter. Then scans for the first and last parseable timestamps to seed the time-range fields and the AI context.

model3d-ui.title: UI
model3d-ui.description: Everything on the 3D tab: the toolbar, the Helix viewport, the stats footer and the material inspector.

model3d-functionality.title: Functionality
model3d-functionality.description: What the viewer does behind the scene: routing a file extension to a loader, tinting materials the file leaves uncoloured, reporting what a file declares but the viewer cannot render, and the camera maths every gesture and AI camera tool shares.

model3d-inspector-toggle.title: Inspector Toggle
model3d-inspector-toggle.description: Right-hand toolbar toggle that shows or hides the material inspector. Present only when the model actually has materials or unrendered elements to show, and opens by default when it does.

model3d-error-overlay.title: Load Error Overlay
model3d-error-overlay.description: Centred message shown in place of geometry when a model cannot be opened - an unregistered extension, a read failure, or a file that parsed but held no renderable mesh.

model3d-stats-format.title: Detected Format
model3d-stats-format.description: The loader-reported format name for the opened file (STL, glTF, FBX, ...).

model3d-stats-counts.title: Geometry Counts
model3d-stats-counts.description: Triangle, vertex and mesh counts plus the file size, so the size of what is on screen is legible without asking the assistant.

model3d-materials.title: Material List
model3d-materials.description: One row per material: name, colour swatch and hex, plus texture detail. Materials the file leaves uncoloured are tinted apart so they stay visually separable.

model3d-unsupported.title: Declared but Not Rendered
model3d-unsupported.description: Lists what the file declares that the viewer does not draw - animations, cameras, lights, skeletal rigs - so a partial render is never mistaken for the whole file.

model3d-camera.title: Camera Maths
model3d-camera.description: The pose arithmetic every camera move shares: orbit about the model, turn about world-up, roll about the line of sight, zoom toward the look-at point, pan across the view plane, and framing a file's authored viewpoint from the model bounds. Pure pose in, pose out - the view only reads and writes the viewport camera.

model3d-tinting.title: Categorical Tinting
model3d-tinting.description: Gives materials a file leaves uncoloured a distinct colour from the theme's Swatch bank, so meshes that would otherwise render identically stay separable in the viewport and the inspector.

model3d-inspection.title: Unrendered Content Report
model3d-inspection.description: Walks a loaded scene for content the viewer does not draw (animations, cameras, lights, rigs) and turns it into the inspector's honest not-rendered list.

images-ui.title: UI
images-ui.description: Everything on the image tab: the top toolbar, the four content surfaces it switches between, the floating image tools, the full-screen window and the right-click menu.

images-functionality.title: Functionality
images-functionality.description: What the viewer does behind the controls: stepping and clamping through the set, timing the slideshow, laying out the collage, loading thumbnails in the background, and the entry points that open images in the first place.

images-toolbar.title: Top Toolbar
images-toolbar.description: Strip across the top of the tab: the segmented sub-view selector on the left, the heading in the middle, and the slideshow + full-screen controls on the right.

images-header.title: Heading
images-header.description: Centre heading: the current file name in the image-led views (carousel and explore), or the image count in the grid views.

images-fullscreen-btn.title: Full-Screen Button
images-fullscreen-btn.description: Opens the current image in the borderless full-screen window.

images-dot-paging.title: Dot Paging
images-dot-paging.description: The forward/back chevrons either side of the dot strip, shown only when the set is longer than one 20-dot block; each jumps a whole block.

images-explore-step.title: Wheel Stepping (image pane)
images-explore-step.description: Wheeling over the right-hand image pane steps the selection through the set, clamped at the ends, keeping the thumbnail strip in sync.

images-collage-panzoom.title: Pan and Zoom
images-collage-panzoom.description: Drag anywhere to pan the canvas; the wheel zooms about the cursor so the point under the pointer stays put. Scale is clamped so the collage can never be lost off-screen or shrunk to nothing.

images-fullscreen-nav.title: Full-Screen Navigation
images-fullscreen-nav.description: Inside the full-screen window: space, click or right-arrow advance, left-arrow and right-click go back, Esc exits and also stops auto-advance. Rotation and the slideshow stay in sync with the tab behind it.

images-context-menu.title: Image Context Menu
images-context-menu.description: Right-click menu offered on the featured image and on every thumbnail. Delete is its only entry today.

images-collage-layout.title: Collage Layout
images-collage-layout.description: Scatters the thumbnails across the canvas with a fixed seed, so re-entering the collage shows the same arrangement rather than reshuffling; the layout is recomputed only when the set itself changes.

audio-ui.title: UI
audio-ui.description: Everything on the player tab: the panel-toggle top bar, the playlist drawer, the now-playing header, the visualisers, the transport row, and the tags / lyrics drawer.

audio-functionality.title: Functionality
audio-functionality.description: What the player does behind the controls: the NAudio engine lifecycle, the play queue, auto-advance, FFT and waveform analysis, .lrc parsing, tag read/write, and the entry points that fill the queue.

audio-topbar.title: Top Bar
audio-topbar.description: Strip across the top of the tab: the playlist drawer toggle on the left, and the background-play, Tags and Lyrics toggles on the right. The Tags/Lyrics pair share one drawer, so pressing the active one closes it.

audio-visuals.title: Visualisers
audio-visuals.description: The middle of the player: the live spectrum bars, the whole-track waveform that doubles as the seek bar, and the position / duration readouts under it.

audio-playlist-toggle.title: Playlist Toggle
audio-playlist-toggle.description: Opens and closes the queue drawer. Shown only for a multi-track queue - there is nothing to list for a single file.

audio-tags-toggle.title: Tags Toggle
audio-tags-toggle.description: Shows the tag editor in the right drawer; pressing it again while it is showing closes the drawer rather than switching to it.

audio-lyrics-toggle.title: Lyrics Toggle
audio-lyrics-toggle.description: Shows the lyrics view in the same right drawer, replacing the tag editor if that was open.

audio-albumart.title: Album Art
audio-albumart.description: The current track's embedded cover, falling back to a music-note placeholder when the file carries none.

audio-trackinfo.title: Track Details
audio-trackinfo.description: Title, artist and album for the current track, falling back to the file name when the tags are empty.

audio-queue-counter.title: Queue Position
audio-queue-counter.description: Position counter (for example 3 / 12), shown only when more than one track is queued.

audio-time-readout.title: Position / Duration
audio-time-readout.description: Elapsed and total time under the waveform, formatted from the engine's position as it plays.

audio-tageditor-fields.title: Tag Fields
audio-tageditor-fields.description: Title, artist, album, year, track, genre and comment boxes. Editing any of them marks the editor dirty, which is what enables Save.

audio-tageditor-save.title: Save Tags
audio-tageditor-save.description: Writes the edited tags back to the file. The playback engine is released first so TagLib can open the file for writing, then the track is reloaded.

audio-lyrics-sync.title: Synced Highlight
audio-lyrics-sync.description: Tracks the playhead through the parsed .lrc lines, highlighting the current line and scrolling it into view; embedded unsynced lyrics render statically and a track with neither shows a plain message.

audio-engine.title: Playback Engine
audio-engine.description: The NAudio engine's life: created lazily on first play, kept alive across tab switches, released before a tag write, and driving a roughly 30fps render tick that feeds the spectrum, the playhead and the lyric highlight.
audio-engine.note: Only the lazy half is unit-testable, and it is the half that breaks: every transport command must be safe before the engine exists, because the tab opens without one. Actually starting audio needs an output device (none headless), so playback itself is left to the UI journey.

audio-queue.title: Play Queue
audio-queue.description: The ordered track list behind the playlist and the transport: which track is current, whether there is a next or previous one, and what reordering or jumping does to that position.

audio-lrc.title: Lyrics Parsing
audio-lrc.description: Reads a sibling .lrc file into timed lines - multiple stamps per line expand to one line each, an offset tag shifts them all, and malformed or id-only lines are skipped rather than failing the load.

audio-waveform-analysis.title: Waveform Analysis
audio-waveform-analysis.description: Reads the whole audio file once to build a normalised peak envelope for the waveform strip; a file it cannot open yields an empty envelope rather than an error.

audio-fft.title: Spectrum Analysis
audio-fft.description: Aggregates playback samples into FFT band magnitudes on the render tick, which is what the spectrum bars draw.

audio-tag-io.title: Tag Read / Write
audio-tag-io.description: Reads ID3 tags and embedded art on load and writes them back on save, through TagLib.

video-ui.title: UI
video-ui.description: Everything on the video tab: the picture and its overlays, the transport bar, the media-info panel, the keyframe scene strip and the fullscreen window.

video-functionality.title: Functionality
video-functionality.description: What the player does behind the controls: standing up and tearing down the libVLC engine, blitting decoded frames into a WPF bitmap, reading the parsed tracks into the info model, sampling keyframes on a second decoder, and the entry point that opens a file.

video-click-pause.title: Click to Play / Pause
video-click-pause.description: An invisible full-area button over the picture, so clicking anywhere on the video toggles playback - the same command the transport button and the centre affordance run.

video-infopanel-toggle.title: Media Info Toggle
video-infopanel-toggle.description: Shows or hides the right-hand codec / metadata panel.

video-scenestrip-toggle.title: Scene Strip Toggle
video-scenestrip-toggle.description: Shows or hides the keyframe strip. The strip only actually appears once keyframes have been sampled, so the toggle can be on with nothing to show.

video-fullscreen-toggle.title: Fullscreen Toggle
video-fullscreen-toggle.description: Opens the borderless fullscreen window; Esc or closing it drops back to the tab.

video-info-sections.title: Track Sections
video-info-sections.description: One section per track group - File, Video, Audio, Subtitles - each a list of label/value rows read from the parsed media.

video-scene-seek.title: Seek to Scene
video-scene-seek.description: Clicking a thumbnail seeks to that scene. If playback has not started yet the seek is deferred until the first frame is up, rather than seeking a decoder with no output.

video-fullscreen-transport.title: Fullscreen Transport
video-fullscreen-transport.description: The same transport-bar template as the tab, bound to the same view-model, so the controls behave identically in both places.
video-fullscreen-transport.note: The same template bound to the same view-model, so its buttons run the very commands asserted on the tab transport leaves - there is no second code path to test. The journey checks it opens and closes.

video-engine.title: Engine Lifecycle
video-engine.description: Builds the libVLC engine and parses the media on a background thread so the tab paints first, re-asserts volume on play (libVLC only builds its audio output once playback starts), and tears everything down on close. A fatal engine error closes the tab with a shell notification rather than leaving a dead picture.
video-engine.note: Standing the engine up needs libVLC natives and a decodable clip, and tearing it down needs one that is running - neither is available headlessly. What the tab is actually exposed to is the window before the engine exists, and that IS tested: every transport command is reachable from a painted tab with no player, and VideoSurfaceTests asserts each one no-ops rather than throwing.

video-sink.title: Frame Sink
video-sink.description: Receives decoded frames from libVLC into a WriteableBitmap the WPF Image binds to - the reason the picture is an ordinary WPF element with no native-window airspace, so overlays and fullscreen are plain WPF.
video-sink.note: The sink is fed by libVLC decode callbacks straight into a WriteableBitmap - there is no input to it without a running decoder, and nothing to read back but pixels. The UI journey covers that a picture appears.

video-mediainfo.title: Media Info Model
video-mediainfo.description: Turns the parsed media's tracks into the sectioned label/value model the info panel and the AI's get_media_info both read.

video-keyframes.title: Keyframe Sampling
video-keyframes.description: Samples about 32 stills evenly across the duration on a separate short-lived decoder, so scrubbing the strip never disturbs playback.
video-keyframes.note: Sampling itself spins up a second libVLC decoder, so only the strip own model - the time labels the thumbnails carry, and the empty-until-sampled state - is unit-tested; the sampling run is left to the UI journey.

video-open.title: Open Actions
video-open.description: The As Video file action that opens common video extensions in the player tab.

scratchpad-ui.title: UI
scratchpad-ui.description: Everything on the board: the toolbar, the infinite canvas and its minimap, the post-it itself, the note mini-ribbon and the recycle-bin panel.

scratchpad-functionality.title: Functionality
scratchpad-functionality.description: What the board does behind the controls: classifying whatever is dropped or pasted into the right kind of note, persisting notes and their attachments, expiring and purging them, and the settings and theme tokens they read.

recycle-delete.title: Delete Permanently
recycle-delete.description: Removes one note from the bin for good, taking its attachment folder with it.

recycle-empty.title: Empty Recycle Bin
recycle-empty.description: The split button dropdown entry that clears the whole bin. Confirmation-gated, because nothing here is recoverable afterwards.

scratchpad-persistence.title: Persistence
scratchpad-persistence.description: Notes live as one file each under the workspace, saved on a debounce as they are edited and moved between the board and the recycle-bin folder rather than rewritten. Each note owns an attachment folder keyed on its id, which follows it through recycle and restore and is removed only on permanent delete.

scratchpad-expiry.title: Expiry and Purge
scratchpad-expiry.description: An unpinned note counts down its configured lifetime and moves itself to the recycle bin when it runs out; pinning clears the expiry entirely. The bin purges anything older than the configured retention on startup.

recycle-list.title: Binned Note List
recycle-list.description: The bin panel lists each binned note by the first non-empty line of its content, truncated, so a board of untitled notes is still navigable.

projects-ui.title: UI
projects-ui.description: Both project surfaces plus the two file-explorer viewlets: the bucketed list page with its summary pane, the per-project detail tab with its backlog board, and the viewlets a project folder grows in the explorer.

projects-functionality.title: Functionality
projects-functionality.description: What sits under the pages: reading and writing the .project file transactionally, the configurable backlog status chain, moving a project between its active / shelf / archive folders, the v2 schema migration, and the per-workspace settings.

projects-viewlets.title: Explorer Viewlets
projects-viewlets.description: What a folder shows in the file explorer once it holds a .project: the backlog status breakdown, and the AI summary editor for a folder .aisummary.

projects-buckets-tabs.title: Bucket Tabs
projects-buckets-tabs.description: Projects / Shelf / Archives tabs; switching one reloads the list from that bucket configured folder.

projects-list-rows.title: Project Rows
projects-list-rows.description: One row per project: its name (falling back to the folder name when the .project does not set one), the first couple of non-empty description lines, and a backlog item count. Empty when the feature is switched off.

projects-summary-markdown.title: Summary Markdown
projects-summary-markdown.description: The selected project read-only description, with a generated Mermaid pie of its backlog status breakdown prepended so the shape of the work is visible without opening it.

projects-open.title: Open Project / Open Files
projects-open.description: Opens the project detail tab, or the project folder in the file explorer - both resolved to an absolute path from the active bucket root.

projects-bucket-actions.title: Archive / Shelf / Reactivate
projects-bucket-actions.description: The bucket button on the summary pane: Archive and Shelf for an active project, Reactivate for one already put away.

projects-detail-tabs.title: Detail Tabs
projects-detail-tabs.description: Project Details / Backlog tabs, opening on Backlog when the project already has a description and on Project Details when it does not - so a new project lands where there is something to write.
projects-detail-tabs.note: Which tab opens first is decided in the page factory from whether the project already has a description, and the tabs themselves are a TabControl. There is no view-model state to read back; the journey opens a project and checks both tabs are reachable.

projects-store.title: Project File Store
projects-store.description: Reading and writing the .project file: listing a bucket, loading one project (naming it after its folder when the file is missing), and every mutation going through a scoped transaction so a half-written file never replaces a good one.

notebook-ui.title: UI
notebook-ui.description: The notebook tab: the cells rendered in document order, and the right-hand code outline beside them.

notebook-functionality.title: Functionality
notebook-functionality.description: What sits under the page: parsing nbformat JSON into ordered cells, resolving the kernel to a tree-sitter grammar, extracting the code structure the outline lists, and the entry point that opens a .ipynb.

notebook-outline-entries.title: Outline Entries
notebook-outline-entries.description: One entry per code cell that declares something, listing its types and top-level functions as markdown. The panel is hidden entirely when a notebook declares nothing, rather than showing an empty column.

notebook-parse.title: nbformat Parsing
notebook-parse.description: Reads the nbformat JSON into ordered cells. Cell source arrives as either a single string or an array of line-strings and is decoded and joined either way; a malformed or unrecognised file yields an empty notebook rather than failing the tab.

notebook-structure.title: Code Structure Extraction
notebook-structure.description: Runs each code cell through the shared tree-sitter structure extractor to collect its declared types and top-level functions, which is what the outline renders.

notebook-open.title: Open Actions
notebook-open.description: The As Notebook file action that opens a .ipynb in the viewer tab.

win-search-ui.title: UI
win-search-ui.description: The results tab: the header saying what was searched and where, the sortable results grid, and the action strip beside it.

win-search-functionality.title: Functionality
win-search-functionality.description: What sits under the tab: parsing the query into an OLE DB WHERE clause, running it against the SystemIndex, deciding the scope, and the scoring that lets the AI question mark handler judge whether a prompt is even a search.

search-result-row.title: Result Row
search-result-row.description: One row per match: the name with a file or folder icon, the location relative to the search root, and size and modified columns that render blank rather than 0 B or an epoch date when the index has no value for them.

search-query-scorer.title: Query Suitability Scoring
search-query-scorer.description: Scores a free-text prompt on how much it looks like a file search rather than a question - globs and property filters and quoted phrases score high, conversational sentences low - so the shell question mark handler knows whether to launch a search at all.

search-refine.title: Query Refinement
search-refine.description: Merging a follow-up query into the running one with AND, so refining a search narrows it instead of starting over. Driven through ISearchable: an explicit '?' forces the refine even mid-search, and because AQS has no regex operator the page declares SupportsRegex=false and refuses a regex outright rather than quietly running it as literal text.

aichat-ui.title: UI
aichat-ui.description: Both AI Chat surfaces: the browser over saved conversations with its analysis overlay, and a single conversation tab with its thread, context strip and preview panel.

aichat-functionality.title: Functionality
aichat-functionality.description: What sits under the two tabs: persisting and resuming conversations within a token budget, the background analysis that summarises one, the retention purge, and the union of pinned pages tools with its security-context disambiguation.

aichat-browser-list.title: Conversation Rows
aichat-browser-list.description: One row per saved conversation: title, the span it covers, its message count and, once the background analysis has run, its summary. A row updates in place when its analysis lands rather than waiting for a refresh.

aichat-browser-filter.title: Date Filter
aichat-browser-filter.description: Today / Last 7 days / This month / This year, filtering on last activity rather than start time so a long-running conversation does not fall out of view. Defaults to the last 7 days.

aichat-analysis-sections.title: Analysis Sections
aichat-analysis-sections.description: Summary, topic, tone and evolution, understanding, key decisions, important facts and valuable attachments - each shown only when the analysis produced one - plus a button that opens the conversation itself.

aichat-thread.title: Message Thread
aichat-thread.description: User and assistant bubbles in order, with live agent activity between them: collapsible tool batches and the typing line. An answer that comes back empty renders a notice rather than a blank bubble, and is not persisted as a message.

aichat-token-footer.title: Token Budget Footer
aichat-token-footer.description: Running estimate of the conversation size against the model's context window, so a conversation approaching its limit is visible before it starts dropping history.
aichat-token-footer.note: A live readout of the running token estimate against the model context window. The budgeting it displays is asserted on aichat-history-resume; the footer itself is two bound numbers with no rule of its own.

aichat-context-chips.title: Context Chips
aichat-context-chips.description: One chip per pinned page, carrying a security-risk badge and a remove button. Pinning the same page twice flashes the existing chip instead of stacking a duplicate; two tabs of the same kind on different targets pin separately.

aichat-context-attachments.title: Attachments
aichat-context-attachments.description: Files pinned alongside the pages, with a marker on any whose file has since gone.
aichat-context-attachments.note: Attachments are a plain path list with a missing-file marker; the content they contribute is assembled and asserted through aichat-ai-context.

aichat-analysis.title: Background Analysis
aichat-analysis.description: Summarises a finished conversation off the UI thread - topic, tone, decisions, facts - and saves it as an artifact beside the record, which is what the browser row and a resumed conversation both read instead of replaying every message.
aichat-analysis.note: Producing an analysis is a real model call on a background queue - a unit test must not make one. What the analysis is FOR is asserted either side of it: aichat-history-resume checks a prior analysis stands in for the messages it covers on resume, and the browser row updates in place when one lands.

aichat-purge.title: Retention Purge
aichat-purge.description: Deletes conversations past the configured retention window when the browser tab opens, keyed on last activity so an old conversation still being used survives.
aichat-purge.note: Shares its last-activity rule with the browser filter (ConversationPurgeTask.LastActivity), which is where that rule is asserted - a conversation is judged by when it was last used, not when it began, so retention never deletes one still in play.

aichat-tool-union.title: Pinned Tool Union
aichat-tool-union.description: The conversation exposes the union of every pinned page's client tools. When the same tool name arrives from two or more distinct security contexts they are wrapped as one tool with a security_context selector, so the model has to say which tab it means rather than silently acting on whichever was pinned first.
aichat-tool-union.note: Exercising it needs two pinned pages that both expose a same-named tool under different security contexts, which means two live page view-models inside a conversation - the journey territory. The readiness and pinning half that decides WHICH pages contribute is asserted in ConversationContextReadinessTests.

aichat-preview-pane.title: Preview Pane
aichat-preview-pane.description: The pane itself: a page that implements IContextPreview renders its own read-only view here; one that does not gets a placeholder showing the exact context text the AI will see, so a page is never previewed as blank. Closing it deselects the chip.

dicom-ui.title: UI
dicom-ui.description: The viewer tab: the contents panel on the left, and on the right the image toolbar, the stage the frame is drawn on, the cine transport under it and the collapsible tag drawer beside it.

dicom-functionality.title: Functionality
dicom-functionality.description: What sits under the tab: recognising DICOM on disk, reading a DICOMDIR / folder / single file / selection into one tree off the UI thread, extracting an encapsulated report to its own viewer, and the file and folder actions that open the tab at all.

dicom-contents-panel.title: Contents Panel
dicom-contents-panel.description: The left column: a Contents header with the container summary and the Hide-patient toggle, over the Patient>Study>Series>Instance tree.

dicom-content-tree.title: Content Tree
dicom-content-tree.description: The Patient>Study>Series>Instance tree. Selecting an image opens it; selecting a container node jumps to the first image beneath it rather than blanking the pane, and the first image is selected automatically on load.

dicom-contents-status.title: Container Summary
dicom-contents-status.description: The line under the Contents header: a non-identifying counts-and-modalities summary once loaded, 'No DICOM content found.' for an empty container, or the reason the read failed.

dicom-toolbar.title: Image Toolbar
dicom-toolbar.description: The row above the stage: framing, invert, the measurement tool picker, Clear, the CT window presets, and the Tags drawer toggle. Everything but the Tags toggle is disabled until an image is selected.

dicom-zoom-buttons.title: Fit / Actual Size
dicom-zoom-buttons.description: Fit scales the image to the stage and centres it; 1:1 puts it back to source pixels, centred, letting an image larger than the stage overflow rather than be clamped to it.

dicom-invert.title: Invert
dicom-invert.description: Inverts the greyscale mapping - a photographic negative of the windowed frame, not a solid flood.

dicom-tool-picker.title: Measurement Tool Picker
dicom-tool-picker.description: Arms one of Pan / Length / Angle / Rect / Ellipse / Probe. The armed tool decides how many clicks the stage collects before it commits an annotation; Pan and Probe collect none.

dicom-clear-measurements.title: Clear Measurements
dicom-clear-measurements.description: Clears the annotations on the current frame only - the other frames' annotations are kept, since they are held per frame.

dicom-wl-presets.title: Window Presets
dicom-wl-presets.description: Bone / Lung / Soft / Brain apply the standard CT window widths and centres; Default restores the window the image itself declared. The active preset highlights, and a manual right-drag drops it to 'custom'.

dicom-tags-toggle.title: Tags Toggle
dicom-tags-toggle.description: Opens the tag drawer for the selected instance. Enabled only when the selection actually has a file behind it, so the drawer never opens onto nothing.

dicom-frame-render.title: Rendered Frame
dicom-frame-render.description: fo-dicom's RawImage rendered to a BGRA32 WriteableBitmap at the current window/level, off the UI thread, with the previous frame left up if a render fails.

dicom-zoom-pan.title: Zoom & Pan
dicom-zoom-pan.description: Ctrl+wheel zooms anchored on the cursor - the pixel under the pointer stays under it - and a left-drag pans while no measurement tool is armed.
dicom-zoom-pan.note: The fit and cursor-anchored zoom live in Visuals.Common's ViewportFit, shared with the SVG canvas - the second surface that had to own its own transform rather than lean on Stretch, because both draw something in screen space over the content.

dicom-series-scroll.title: Series Scroll
dicom-series-scroll.description: A plain wheel steps through the slices of the current series, clamped at both ends rather than wrapping, keeping the window/level and zoom that were already set.

dicom-probe.title: Pixel / HU Probe
dicom-probe.description: Hover readout of the raw stored value at a pixel, converted to Hounsfield units when the image carries a rescale slope and intercept.

dicom-overlays.title: Corner Overlays
dicom-overlays.description: Modality, dimensions, the live window/level and the frame position top-left; the patient line top-right, which the Hide-patient toggle removes; the probe readout bottom-left.

dicom-cine-play.title: Play / Pause
dicom-cine-play.description: Runs the frames on a timer, wrapping at the end. Starting cine on a single-frame image does nothing.
dicom-cine-play.note: The timer ticking is a dispatcher loop no unit test has, so what is asserted is the state around it: cine stops when another image opens, and the transport is not shown at all for a single-frame image.

dicom-cine-step.title: Step Frame
dicom-cine-step.description: Next and previous frame, wrapping at both ends - unlike the series scroll, which clamps, because a loop is what a cine sequence is.

dicom-cine-slider.title: Frame Slider
dicom-cine-slider.description: Scrubs directly to a frame; moving it re-renders and re-points the annotation set at that frame's.

dicom-tag-list.title: Tag List
dicom-tag-list.description: Group/element, name, VR and value for every tag on the instance, with the identifying values masked while Hide-patient is on.

dicom-tag-filter.title: Tag Filter
dicom-tag-filter.description: Narrows the list as you type, matching against the tag id, the name or the value - so '0010' and 'Modality' and a value fragment all find their row.

dicom-tag-copy.title: Copy Tag Menu
dicom-tag-copy.description: Right-click a row to copy its value, its name, its tag id, or the whole row as tab-separated text for a spreadsheet.
dicom-tag-copy.note: Four menu items that put a string on the Windows clipboard. There is no rule between the row and the clipboard to get wrong - and a test that takes the clipboard is a test that interferes with whatever else the machine is doing. The drawer's own behaviour is covered on dicom-tag-list and dicom-tag-filter.

dicom-sniffer.title: DICOM Detection
dicom-sniffer.description: Recognising DICOM on disk. A study CD routinely stores instances with no extension at all, so the authoritative test is the DICM marker at byte 128 rather than the file name; the extension is only the cheap first guess.

dicom-open-actions.title: Open Actions
dicom-open-actions.description: How the tab is reached: 'As DICOM' on one or more matched files, and the same on a folder that holds a DICOMDIR or any .dcm - offered on a drive root too, because a study CD is opened from its drive.

dicom-ai-context.title: Context - get_context
dicom-ai-context.description: Reports the container title, its non-identifying summary, and the currently viewed image's modality, series, body part, geometry, frame position and window/level - and names the tools that go further. Patient name, ID and date of birth are withheld whatever the Hide-patient toggle is set to.

dicom-ai-act.title: Act - client tools
dicom-ai-act.description: Read-only viewer parity: list the study, display an image, read its tags, step frames, and capture what is on screen. Every tool is a safe operation - nothing here writes, and nothing reaches patient identifiers.

dicom-ai-act-list-contents.title: dicom_list_contents
dicom-ai-act-list-contents.description: Lists each series with its modality, description, body part and image count, plus the 1-based index range to pass to dicom_view_image. No patient identifiers.

dicom-ai-act-view-image.title: dicom_view_image
dicom-ai-act-view-image.description: Selects and renders a specific image by 1-based index so it can then be captured. An index outside the container is an error, not a silent clamp.

dicom-ai-act-current-info.title: dicom_get_current_image_info
dicom-ai-act-current-info.description: Reports what is on screen right now: modality, series, geometry, frame position, window/level and transfer syntax.

dicom-ai-act-read-tags.title: dicom_read_tags
dicom-ai-act-read-tags.description: The instance's DICOM tags, optionally filtered, capped at 250 rows with the remainder counted. Always de-identified - the UI's Hide-patient toggle does not widen what the model sees.

dicom-ai-act-next-frame.title: dicom_next_frame
dicom-ai-act-next-frame.description: Advances a multi-frame image by one and reports the new position.

dicom-ai-act-prev-frame.title: dicom_prev_frame
dicom-ai-act-prev-frame.description: Steps a multi-frame image back one and reports the new position.

dicom-ai-act-capture.title: dicom_capture_image
dicom-ai-act-capture.description: Encodes the displayed frame at its current window/level as a PNG and attaches it, so the model looks at what the user is looking at rather than at a re-render of its own.
dicom-ai-act-capture.note: The PNG encode itself is a PngBitmapEncoder over a live WriteableBitmap - an STA render, not a unit test. What is asserted is that the tool is offered and declared a safe operation; that the pixels are the ones on screen follows from it encoding CurrentBitmap rather than re-rendering.

dicom-ai-preview.title: Preview - IContextPreview
dicom-ai-preview.description: IContextPreview is not implemented (no feature is yet). A read-only preview would let the conversation context panel show the current frame without re-hosting the live viewer.
dicom-ai-preview.note: IContextPreview not implemented (no feature is yet). A narrow read-only preview would let the conversation context panel show this page without re-hosting the live view.

console-ui.title: UI
console-ui.description: The Console tab: the live terminal surface with its path bar, the Files / Environment / History panels flanking it, and the overlays and config editor through which environments are chosen and edited.

console-functionality.title: Functionality
console-functionality.description: What sits under the tab: deciding whether a typed line is a shell command or a question for the assistant, the named per-location environments a shell launches with, and the folder action that opens a console rooted anywhere.

console-vt-screen.title: Screen & Scrollback
console-vt-screen.description: The VT screen with cursor-positioned output applied, and the lines that scroll off its top kept as scrollback. What is on the visible grid stays in the snapshot; only evicted lines become history.

console-path-bar.title: Path Bar & Busy Indicator
console-path-bar.description: The current directory above the terminal, re-read from the shell's own prompt rather than tracked separately, and a 'running.' indicator that lights while a command is in flight and clears on Ctrl-C or the next prompt.

console-env-surfaces.title: Environment Surfaces
console-env-surfaces.description: The three places environments are chosen or edited: the per-variable add/edit overlay, the launch picker that asks which environment a new location should use, and the config editor in the workspace Configure overlay.

win-file-system-functionality.title: Functionality
win-file-system-functionality.description: What sits under the tab: the ready-made named-folder tab variants, resolving which experience a file opens in, and the path-navigation query handler that drives the active tab from the AI bar.

winfs-overlays.title: Modal Overlays
winfs-overlays.description: The prompts that cover the page: the danger-styled confirmation used before a permanent delete, the single-field input prompt used for rename, and the multi-step Define New association wizard.

winfs-config-editors.title: Options Editors
winfs-config-editors.description: The two Options pages behind the action strip: the external-app launch definitions, and the file-type-to-experience map that decides what a double-click opens.

winfs-default-open.title: Default-Open Resolution
winfs-default-open.description: Which experience a file opens in: criteria matched by extension, compound extension, perceived type, content type or magic number, with a more specific path rule beating a general one. Seeded from the bundled default filemap, which merges forward on an update rather than overwriting what the user changed.

hex-functionality.title: Functionality
hex-functionality.description: What sits under the tab: the windowed piece-table buffer that keeps memory bounded whatever the file size, the byte edit operations and their history, and the action that opens a binary here in the first place.

hex-toolbar.title: Toolbar
hex-toolbar.description: The row above the surface: the edit-mode toggles and Go To on the left with undo/redo and the Save split button, the encoding selector and the evaluation-pane toggle on the right.

hex-edit-ops.title: Byte Edit Operations
hex-edit-ops.description: Overwrite, insert and delete against the piece table, each recorded so it can be reversed in order. An edit lives in the add buffer until Save writes it back, which is what lets an edited byte be drawn differently from an original one.

hex-open-actions.title: Open Actions
hex-open-actions.description: 'As Binary' - the file action that opens anything in the hex editor, and the fallback the file map resolves to when nothing more specific claims a file.

json-functionality.title: Functionality
json-functionality.description: What sits under the tab: reading a file into a tree - streaming a large one through a byte-offset index rather than holding it all - evaluating a JSONPath against that tree, and the action that opens a .json here.

json-toolbar.title: Toolbar
json-toolbar.description: View-mode toggles for the selected node on the left, Format and the Save button - which only appears once something has been changed - on the right.

json-display-list.title: Display List
json-display-list.description: A flat, virtualizing row list backed by the tree model - the viewer proper. The selected node renders in one of three mutually-exclusive modes, and only the rows in view are ever realised.

json-open-actions.title: Open Actions
json-open-actions.description: 'As Json' - the file action for the /text/json experience. One file at a time: the viewer holds one document.

svg-functionality.title: Functionality
svg-functionality.description: What sits under the tab: parsing .svg or .svgz into a frozen drawing off the UI thread, holding the AI back until that has happened, and the action that opens a vector file here.

svg-toolbar.title: Toolbar
svg-toolbar.description: Reset view and the checkerboard toggle, with a hint that the wheel zooms and a drag pans.

svg-reset-view.title: Reset View
svg-reset-view.description: Refits the artwork to the window and re-centres it - the way back after zooming into a corner.

svg-checkerboard.title: Checkerboard Toggle
svg-checkerboard.description: Puts a checkerboard behind the art instead of a flat theme background. On by default, because vector art is usually transparent and against a plain backdrop transparent is indistinguishable from white.

svg-canvas.title: Canvas
svg-canvas.description: The artwork itself: fitted to the window on first show, then wheel-zoomed about the cursor and drag-panned. Zooming re-tessellates the vector drawing rather than scaling a bitmap, so it stays crisp at any magnification; the pan only begins once the pointer has actually moved, so a click still behaves like a click.
svg-canvas.note: The wheel-zoom shares Visuals.Common's PanZoomMiniMap.ZoomAt with the collage and the corkboard, and the fit shares ViewportFit with the DICOM stage - so 'the point under the cursor stays put' and 'fit letterboxes and centres' are asserted once, in Tests.Core, for every surface that has them. What is left here is the drag threshold, which is a mouse gesture against a live canvas.

svg-error-overlay.title: Error Overlay
svg-error-overlay.description: Replaces the art with the reason it is not there: unreadable, too large to render safely, or parsed but containing nothing to draw. A blank canvas with no message reads as a broken viewer rather than a broken file.

svg-footer.title: Metadata Footer
svg-footer.description: The file's declared width and height, its viewBox where it has one, the drawable-element count and the file size. Declared size and viewBox can disagree, and which you are looking at decides whether the art is as its author intended.

svg-load-gate.title: Load Gate
svg-load-gate.description: Rendering happens after the tab paints, so the AI send gate is held until the load finishes - and released even when it fails, or a broken file would leave the conversation waiting for a page that never arrives. Files past 64 MB are refused rather than rendered, since a pathological SVG expands into an unbounded visual tree.

svg-open-actions.title: Open Actions
svg-open-actions.description: 'As SVG' - the file action that opens a vector file in the viewer.

json-streaming-format.title: Streaming Re-indent
json-streaming-format.description: Re-indent the file by streaming it - Utf8JsonReader straight into a Utf8JsonWriter, temp file, atomic replace - rather than serialising the loaded tree. Bounded memory at any file size, and it needs no tree at all, so it lifts the half of the windowed-document guard that currently blocks Format.

json-splice-save.title: Splice Save
json-splice-save.description: Save a windowed document by splicing rather than re-serialising: a piece table over (original file + an add buffer) where every untouched item is copied through byte-for-byte and only edited subtrees emit new bytes, streamed to a temp file and atomically replaced - the OverlayTextFile pattern the Text viewer already uses. Reordering siblings becomes a reordering of pieces, so it costs nothing on a huge array. Needs node-to-byte-range tracking below the current sparse depth-1 index (an edit would imply a load) and separator handling at the splice seams, and the generic overlay should come out of OverlayTextFile first so IO.Common holds one piece table rather than two.
json-splice-save.note: Until this exists, Save refuses while any part of the document is unloaded (json-edit-save) - the only correct behaviour for the current design, since writing the loaded tree would truncate everything unread. This lifts the restriction; it does not fix a defect.

email-ui.title: UI
email-ui.description: The message tab: the envelope header with the raw header list folded away behind it, the body-view toolbar, the body itself on its own surface, and the attachment strip along the bottom.

email-functionality.title: Functionality
email-functionality.description: What sits under the tab: parsing .eml and .msg into one shared document, exposing the attachments as virtual-filesystem entries so each opens in its own viewer, and the action that opens a message here at all.

email-envelope.title: Envelope Header
email-envelope.description: From, To, Cc, Subject and the local-time date. Cc is dropped from the layout entirely when the message has none, rather than showing an empty field.

email-raw-headers.title: Raw Header List
